comments.author: Alex Kim
comments.body: Production error rate for this path dropped to zero after deploy. Closing.

content.text: Production error rate for this path dropped to zero after deploy. Closing.
POST /v2/issues and PATCH due-date paths return HTTP 500 when the due date string fails ISO-8601 parsing. Clients treat 500 as a platform outage and retry, amplifying load.

Invalid values like 2025-13-40 or 2025-04-31T25:00:00Z should yield 422 with a field error on dueDate. Actual response is an unhandled time.Parse panic recovered as a generic 500 with request id only.

Cause hypothesis: parseDueDate sits behind the service layer after auth and rate limiting, and its error is not mapped through the validation error type that the HTTP layer turns into 422. Only the happy-path time.Time conversion is tested.
SDK users and third-party integrators surface noisy outage alerts for what is simply bad input.
